profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, RagingWire CA1 (now branded NTT Sacramento CA1), is located at 1200 Striker Ave., Sacramento, CA 95834. The operator publishes 85,000 square feet of data floor (technical) space and 12.6 megawatts of critical IT load for this specific building; no formal certifications or an opening year are stated on this page. CA1 is one of three buildings NTT operates on its Sacramento campus alongside CA2 and CA3, which the operator's campus overview page describes as totaling 52.7 megawatts of combined critical IT load.

Data center demand is a live capacity-planning issue for the Sacramento Municipal Utility District, the region's dominant electric provider. SMUD held a special board informational session in February 2026 on a surge of data center developer inquiries in the Sacramento region, a briefing that named NTT among the operators seeking service in the area, ahead of any formal service-agreement decisions; SMUD has said it is actively assessing how to accommodate large new loads without compromising grid reliability for existing customers. Sacramento's data center submarket, anchored by NTT's three-building CA1/CA2/CA3 campus, has grown alongside Silicon Valley and Santa Clara as one of Northern California's established colocation hubs, distinct from the newer hyperscale build-out concentrated in markets like Northern Virginia and Texas.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
RagingWire CA1 is one building in a 52.7 MW Sacramento campus operated by NTT, a global telecommunications and IT services company. The operator publishes total campus capacity but not per-building breakdowns, so CA1's own power draw is unknown. If this building represents a third of the campus, a reasonable assumption given the three-building layout, it would be roughly 17.5 MW of total facility power. At 4 MW of IT load per 100 MW of facility capacity, a typical ratio, that would be approximately 4.4 MW of IT load, or roughly 110 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density.

The Sacramento campus holds no published certifications visible in operator specifications. The site sits in California, which has 11 facilities with published megawatt figures totaling 365 MW across 103 mapped locations. The campus ranks twelfth by published capacity in the state, below the top ten but ahead of many smaller deployments.

This campus matters to AI scaling primarily as part of California's constrained total published capacity. The state's grid is the binding constraint on further AI deployment in the region, and a 17.5 MW building in the second-tier tier of Sacramento capacity contributes modestly to that constraint. Whether CA1 serves AI workloads, general cloud compute, or other purposes remains unpublished.
